title: Pixel2Motion - AI Logo Animation Skill
creator: nolangz

verification.method: cloned repo and read source on 2026-10-10

motion_techniques: split-fill draw-on across self-intersections with tip glint
reveal_mechanism: Brief-driven choreography on semantic SVG parts (CSS keyframes or JS act timeline) landing on a QA-verified final vector; draw-on, staggered assembly, scale-pop, mask wipe, morph, letter cascade patterns
motion_family: Disney-12-principles logo choreography with personality-derived easing tokens
concept: Raster logo to minimal smooth SVG (smoothness gate, overlay IoU, 10-iteration budget) structured as addressable parts, then choreographed into a dependency-free HTML showcase with deterministic ?t= seeking, frame strips, easing probe, ink-delta continuity sweep and a final-frame contract.
prompt_excerpt: Use $pixel2motion to turn this raster logo into a clean minimal vector and then into a choreographed logo animation. Analyze the source and write a motion brief (3 brand personality words, usage context, choreography sketch)... (agents/openai.yaml default_prompt, a Codex file)

observations.text: SKILL.md states: 'minimal smooth geometry IS animatable geometry' and enforces a hard Smoothness Gate over IoU.
Motion QA uses deterministic ?t=<ms> seeking, frame strips, an easing probe (computed values at seeked times) and an ink-delta sweep across handoffs.
Final Frame Contract: captured final frame must equal the verified static SVG; same-pipeline ?static=1 vs ?t=<end> must be exact 0 diff.
motion-personality.md maps energy x tone axes to six presets with token sets (duration, ease-enter, ease-settle, squash, overshoot).

docs/index.html labels showcase columns 'Claude' and 'GPT'; README alt text 'Claude Horizon logo motion preview'; two Claude cells note '1 more round prompt after result'. Model and harness are not stated.
README calls it an 'open-source Codex and Claude skill'; SKILL.md is described as Codex-facing and agents/openai.yaml is a Codex file.
Chromium-specific finding: var() timing functions inside @keyframes are silently dropped, degrading motion to linear; skill mandates literal cubic-bezier in keyframes.
Fitting quality depends on the agent hand-fitting Beziers within 10 iterations; trace output is only a starter.
README (fetched): MIT; 2.4k stars; 'open-source Codex and Claude skill'; README does not say demos were Claude-made (only 'claude' in GIF filenames).

SKILL.md (raw, fetched): write 3 personality words + usage context first; durations: splash 1200-2000 ms, header 300-800 ms, hover 150-300 ms; 20/50/30 anticipation/action/follow-through; stagger parts 10-20%; keyframe easing must be literal cubic-bezier (var() silently falls back to linear).
Failure modes documented: stair-stepped trace hidden by high IoU; round-cap stall and pop; lockstep motion; mid-flight clipping; non-deterministic screenshots.
Attribution caveat: demo columns are labelled Claude vs GPT, but model version, harness and prompts are not stated.

transferable_principles: Structure artwork for motion first: one addressable element per semantic part, split along animation seams, stable ids.
Derive motion parameters from a written brief (personality words, energy x tone, usage context) and record the derivation.
Final-frame contract: the animation must land exactly on the verified static logo.
Evidence over claims: deterministic time-seek, frame strips viewed by vision, numeric probes for dropped easing and handoff stalls.
Prefer smooth low-complexity geometry over pixel-fit scores; cap fitting iterations and disclose residuals.
Timeline grammar: anticipation/action/settle about 20/50/30 with staggered overlaps.
Motion brief traces to every parameter
Final animated frame must equal verified static logo
Never let all parts start/stop on the same frame
Seek time (?t=) for QA instead of wall-clock
weaknesses: Very long SKILL.md (28 KB) with many named rules; high load for the agent (observed).
macOS-biased Chrome paths in render_overlay.py and export_claude_videos.mjs (observed).
README publishing checklist stale (says add a LICENSE although one exists) and README is partly commercial marketing (observed).
No final-quality automatic vectorisation; quality relies on agent hand-fitting (observed).
Web/video output only; no Lottie export (observed).
Prompts for the Claude-labelled showcase outputs are not published (observed).
Rigour is overkill for simple single-shape logos (inferred).
Heavy pipeline; needs Chrome/Playwright
Trace output unusable as final art

title: Wiggle - Logo Animation Skill for Claude Code
creator: talknerdytome-labs

verification.method: cloned repo and read source on 2026-10-10

reveal_mechanism: Opacity/scale/position/rotation keyframes on Lottie image layers (PNG assets), with icon and text layers optionally staggered by 15/30/45 frames
motion_family: Lottie image-layer keyframe presets chosen by intent classification
concept: Philosophy-first workflow (personality, emotion, motion metaphor), logo structure analysis, asset preparation, hand-written Lottie JSON, validation scripts (structure, loop, promise-vs-implementation), preview then full render to GIF/MP4.
prompt_excerpt: Animate my logo with a bounce entrance effect

observations.text: SKILL.md makes 'Define Motion Philosophy' and 'Analyze Logo Structure' mandatory 30-second steps before any animation.
Logo text must be extracted from the SVG; recreating it with PIL ImageDraw is listed as a critical mistake.
Animation is applied to rasterised PNG image layers; stroke reveal needs shape layers and is 'Not recommended for first-time users'.
prepare_logo.py imports only Pillow (no SVG rasteriser) although SKILL.md instructs running it on SVG elements; requirements.txt lacks an SVG renderer.
Validation is structural (validate_lottie, validate_loop, verify_animation); no step instructs viewing rendered frames.
references/real-world-examples contains nine third-party brand hover Lottie files (Reddit, Slack, Discord...); redistribution rights unstated, Slack file name suggests an icon-library asset.
README says 'Created for use with Claude Code' but the repo ships no showcase outputs, so no claim of Claude-made output exists.
Hand-writing dense keyframe JSON (25-45+, up to 120 keyframes) without a visual check is error-prone for an agent.
README (fetched): 26 stars, 3 forks; credits line says 'Created for use with Claude Code by Anthropic' and 'part of the Anthropic Agent Skills collection' - I could not confirm this claim.
Example prompts: 'Make my logo wiggle when it appears', 'Add a professional fade-in effect to my brand logo'.

transferable_principles: Make a motion philosophy (personality, emotion, metaphor) a mandatory step before any keyframe.
Analyse logo structure first and branch the workflow (text vs icon, single vs multi-element, vector vs raster).
Never recreate logo text; extract it from the source artwork.
Preview cheaply (first N frames, small test render) before full render, and validate loop closure mathematically.
Verify promise vs implementation (is the stagger actually present?), and add a visual check on top.
Keep SKILL.md a lean index with detail in references, plus size budgets per use case.
Preview only the first ~60 frames while iterating
Check outputs for blank/corrupt renders
Provide size targets per use case
weaknesses: SVG preparation path appears unsupported by prepare_logo.py and requirements (observed).
Raster image-layer animation only; no path-level draw-on or morph in the shipped workflow (observed).
No visual verification of the rendered output (observed).
Dangling reference: text guide points to 'Pattern #9 in SKILL.md', which does not exist (observed).
Cairo GIF rendering crashes on embedded images over 100 KB (observed, documented).
Licence file is an abbreviated Apache-2.0 notice with no copyright holder; third-party brand examples have unclear rights (observed).
README claims Claude Code handles all dependencies automatically, unsupported by SKILL.md (observed).
Single visible commit dated 2025-10-19 in a shallow clone; maintenance cadence unknown (inferred).
Menu of generic effects (fade/bounce/pulse) - low brand specificity (inferred)
Authorship claim in README unverified
license: Apache-2.0 (abbreviated notice in LICENSE.txt, 'Copyright 2025', no holder named, full text not included)

Distil lessons from each round into imperative skill rules, keeping client-specific rules out of the generic skill.
Each shot needs a one-sentence verb action; one evolving idea beats a list of effects.
Inspect crops at full resolution; downscaled sheets hide defects.

title: Animation principles in logo animation (Motion Design School)

reveal_mechanism: Applies classic animation principles to logo motion
concept: Different organisation from School of Motion. Search summary says it covers easing, arcs, squash and stretch.

observations.text: Search summary: even a little easing improves perceived quality; spring/bounce suits playful brands; overuse looks unpolished; rough duration bands 0.3-0.8 s energetic, 1-2 s professional, 2-4 s luxury - the bands came from a skill file, not a recognised authority.

transferable_principles: Ease everything
Arcs for organic paths
Secondary elements settle after primary
weaknesses: Duration bands are a rule of thumb
